weekly.label: Weekly
weekly.title: AI/Agent Weekly Synthesis — 2026-05-15
highlights: Anthropic again had the clearest multi-surface movement, and the required Anthropic surfaces were explicitly checked before concluding scope: [anthropic.com/news](https://www.anthropic.com/news), [claude.com](https://claude.com/), [docs.anthropic.com](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/home), the [Claude Platform release notes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview), the [Claude Managed Agents overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), the [advisor tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool), the [Claude Code docs overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), and the [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog). This week did have important Anthropic platform changes.

On **May 11, 2026**, Anthropic’s [Claude Platform release notes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview) added **Claude Platform on AWS**, exposing Messages, Files, Message Batches, Claude Managed Agents, Agent Skills, code execution, and tool use through Anthropic-managed AWS endpoints with AWS billing and IAM authentication. On **May 12, 2026**, the same surface added **fast mode support for Claude Opus 4.7**. These are not minor SDK notes; they extend the provider’s deployment and latency-control surfaces.

Anthropic’s hosted-agent path remains materially active. The same release-notes surface still shows the **May 6, 2026** launch of **Managed Agent multiagent sessions, outcomes, webhooks, vault refresh, and richer session/event filtering**, and the [Managed Agents overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) now clearly presents agent, environment, session, and events as the core runtime contract. The [advisor tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool) remain live, but I did not find a newer in-window dated advisor launch after the **April 9, 2026** beta; the current doc still centers executor/advisor pairings around Opus 4.7.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: AI Agent Daily Radar - 2026-05-20
highlights: **Google opened its managed-agent harness directly in the Gemini API on May 19, 2026.** In [Introducing Managed Agents in the Gemini API](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/managed-agents-gemini-api/) (**May 19, 2026**), Google says a single call can provision an isolated Linux environment where the Antigravity agent can reason, use tools, execute code, browse the web, and resume with persistent state. The same post explicitly uses `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md` as versionable agent-definition files.

**OpenAI pushed Codex closer to governed enterprise environments on May 18, 2026.** In [OpenAI and Dell Technologies partner to bring Codex to hybrid and on-premises enterprise environments](https://openai.com/index/dell-codex-enterprise-partnership/) (**May 18, 2026**), OpenAI frames Codex as an agent layer that should sit near codebases, docs, business systems, operational knowledge, and team workflows, not just in a cloud coding sandbox.

**OpenAI also expanded the operator-control surface for long-running Codex work on May 14, 2026.** [Work with Codex from anywhere](https://openai.com/index/work-with-codex-from-anywhere/) (**May 14, 2026**) and the matching [ChatGPT Enterprise & Edu release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10128477-chatgpt-enterprise-edu-release-notes%252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525253F.csv) (**May 14, 2026**) add mobile supervision plus enterprise access tokens for trusted, non-interactive local workflows.

artifacts.title: HU-001 — `docs/research/` became the default durable knowledge surface

threads.core_question: How do Radar, Feedback, Knowledge, Proposals, and Implementation stay connected across multiple sessions without treating Harness, radar automation, or the knowledge surface as isolated systems?
threads.current_view: `erwin` should operate as a five-layer knowledge-to-action loop: Radar and Feedback feed Knowledge, mature Knowledge feeds Proposals, reviewed Proposals feed Implementation, and Implementation results flow back into Feedback and Knowledge. Harness is the main implementation target and feedback source, not a shortcut around the loop.
threads.update_when: cross-session handoff fails, stale guidance sends work to the wrong layer, or a new surface changes how the five layers interact

threads.core_question: How does `erwin` keep durable knowledge legible instead of falling back into `docs/research/`, proposal spam, or session-memory dependence?
threads.current_view: The knowledge system must stay file-backed and proposal-gated: repeated usage pressure becomes feedback cases first, active durable understanding lives in `knowledge/`, and only mature threads should create proposal pressure.
threads.update_when: a new case shows the loop being bypassed, or a weekly synthesis/proposal cannot be traced back to a durable thread

threads.core_question: What do first-party and paper evidence together imply about coding-agent self-improvement, and how should `erwin` watch that theme without cargo-culting vendors?
threads.current_view: OpenAI currently presents self-improvement as eval-backed research engineering, Anthropic presents it more as strong internal dogfooding and workflow automation, and the paper-watch archive now has recurring notes for self-correction, long-horizon degradation, context retrieval, and trajectory diagnosis instead of only one starter note.
threads.update_when: a major benchmark shifts, or weekly synthesis finds stronger convergence between vendor claims and papers

threads.thread: harness engineering as legibility + eval pressure
threads.core_question: Which outside signals should turn into eval/doc pressure rather than direct runtime expansion?
threads.current_view: The strongest immediate reusable lesson from recent field signal is not to widen `Harness` runtime blindly, but to keep repo-readable truth, traceability, eval integrity, bounded policy discipline, and monitorability ahead of speculative feature churn. Internal audits, runtime feedback, and newer external monitoring signal now sharpen that thread by showing where visible productization still outruns deeper governance maturity and observability.
threads.update_when: repeated internal gaps show current docs/evals are not making the system legible enough, or new first-party evidence sharpens the eval pattern

threads.core_question: When benchmark-heavy external signal enters the repo, how should `erwin` separate capability signal from eval-trust signal before it sharpens proposal pressure?
threads.current_view: Benchmark-rich signal is now strong enough that the repo needs a durable distinction between “this result highlights a real weakness” and “this benchmark remains a trustworthy measure,” especially when infrastructure setup and output-only reporting can distort what the score seems to mean.
threads.update_when: a weekly synthesis, paper-watch note, or proposal relies heavily on benchmark results that could carry contamination, infrastructure, or gameability risk
